traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and explicit requirements for Story 021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX are implemented and verified:
- **File-Level Template (REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER)**: `ensureFileSupportsAnnotation` + `insertSupportsTemplate` insert a file-level `@supports` JSDoc block when missing, using a default template `@supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ` plus a clear TODO line. Tests assert the exact before/after output. - **Format Fixes (REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT)**: `normalizeReqPrefixInDescription` and `normalizeReqId` normalize malformed `[REQ-...]` prefixes (extra spaces, underscores, parentheses, lowercase) into canonical `[REQ-XXX]` form. Multiple jest tests validate each scenario with expected fixed output. - **Safety & No Inference (REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE)**: Auto-fix is only offered when an existing REQ identifier is present in the test name; otherwise only a diagnostic is reported (see test case with `it('missing prefix', ...)` which has no `output`). Story paths in the inserted template are fixed placeholders; the rule never derives real paths or IDs from context. - **Formatting Preservation (REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE)**: File-level insertion is purely comment text inserted before existing code (respecting shebang), and `createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw` preserves original quote style and escaping when updating test descriptions. No test implementation code is modified—only annotations/strings. - **Integration & UX**: The rule is `fixable: "code"`, wired into the plugin’s main export and presets, and documented in `user-docs/api-reference.md` with explicit mention of Story 021.0 and its auto-fix behaviors. Jest RuleTester-based tests confirm behavior under ESLint’s `--fix` flow.
Given the concrete implementation, targeted tests that pass, and updated documentation, this story is fully implemented and satisfies its definition of done.
